Colombian Government Seizes Oil Facilities Amid Security Crackdown, Impacting Ecopetrol SA

Colombia’s oil and gas producers are grappling with major disruptions after the government initiated a sweeping seizure of key production sites in response to escalating security concerns in the Arauca and Putumayo regions. The crackdown, which began late Tuesday, is affecting operations at several facilities, including those operated by Ecopetrol SA, the nation’s largest oil company.

The move follows weeks of heightened tensions between government forces and armed groups accused of targeting critical energy infrastructure. Authorities say the seizures are a temporary but necessary measure to safeguard assets and personnel. “Our priority is to protect the lives of workers and the integrity of national resources,” Energy Minister Luis Rojas said in a press briefing. “These interventions are under constant review and will remain in place as long as the threat persists.”

Ecopetrol SA confirmed that production has been halted at three of its sites, representing an estimated 35,000 barrels per day—roughly 8% of its daily output. Smaller producer Andes Norte Oil also reported access restrictions at its main field, though it declined to provide figures. “We are cooperating fully with authorities and have evacuated all non-essential staff,” an Ecopetrol spokesperson stated.

Industry analysts estimate the broader sector may lose up to 60,000 barrels per day as a result of the ongoing government action, with potential knock-on effects for Colombia’s export revenues. “The uncertainty is significant,” said Laura García, a Bogotá-based energy consultant. “A prolonged blockade could strain supply chains and investment confidence.”

Union leaders have urged the government to prioritize dialogue to avoid long-term damage. As of Wednesday afternoon, there was no timeline for lifting the seizures, and negotiations between officials and industry representatives were ongoing.
